summary: API gateway feedback-amplification: throttling triggers upstream overload and bursty 502/503s
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (multiple tenants on Dedicated pool) observed an abrupt increase in 502/503 responses from the Redwood API gateway starting ~2026-03-14T11:18Z. Error bursts are correlated with a mixed workload: many long-lived streaming sessions (chat) interleaved with high-rate synchronous generate calls.

Impact:
- Intermittent failures for real-time chat (stream disconnects) and sync generation calls for several enterprise tenants, highest impact on Acme Retail (dedicated pool).
- Elevated error rates (~8% 5xx for the pool) causing customer escalations and automated page.
- Some downstream retries caused increased token/billing accounting anomalies (inflation of billed requests).

Environment:
- Prod dedicated pool: dp-prod-7 (us-east-1)
- API Gateway cluster: apigw-prod-eu/us-east frontends
- Serving runtime: rtm-v2.6 optimized for mixed-batching

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start ~200 concurrent streaming sessions that maintain open HTTP/2 streams for >90s (chat).
2) Inject short sync bursts of 500 requests/sec for 30s from the same tenant.
3) Observe rising queue latencies at the gateway, then a cascade: gateway begins conservative throttling (429), clients retry with backoff disabled -> many attempt new connections -> connection churn and keepalive socket exhaustion -> runtime reports high KV cache churn and OOM-like watchdogs -> runtime process restarts -> gateway returns 502/503 to clients.

Observed behavior:
- Gateway logs show rapidly growing pending request queues and a ramp of 429 followed by 502/503 when upstream disconnects.
- Runtime worker logs show repeated prefix eviction messages and CUDA memory fragmentation warnings immediately preceding process exit.
- Autoscaler did not react quickly due to conservative cooldown and prefetch locks.

Expected behavior:
- Gateway should shed load gracefully without inducing retry storms that create additional connection churn.
- Runtime should be resilient to transient connection bursts (prefer queueing with backpressure signals rather than failfast restarts).

Initial hypothesis:
- A feedback amplification loop: gateway-side throttling triggers client retries/connection churn that increase runtime memory pressure (KV cache and prefetch), triggering runtime restarts and therefore 502/503 at the gateway.
- Long-lived streaming sessions hold kv-cache entries and GPU memory longer, increasing fragmentation during sync burst prefetch.

Mitigation in place (so far):
- Support changed gateway rate-limit rule for impacted tenant to a slightly higher steady quota to avoid immediate 429 cascade (temporary).
- Implemented short-term connection cap per-IP at edge to limit churn (applied 2026-03-14T12:05Z).
- Enabled fallback route to a lower-memory model variant for Acme Retail to reduce runtime OOM probability.

Next steps:
- Engineering to run controlled repro in staging tuned to reproduce mix (SRE + Runtime team).
- Evaluate gateway token-bucket settings to add jittered 429 backoff headers and advisories for clients.
- Consider runtime KV cache eviction policy change to prefer LRU of long-lived streaming prefixes under burst.
- Short-term: keep fallback routing for affected tenants until patch.

12:00 - Replayed traffic in staging with identical mix; reproduced OOM after 27s of sync burst when concurrent streaming sessions >150.

comments: 2026-03-14T11:55Z - Support (Aisha): Customer reported increased 502s ~11:20Z. Triage started; paging SRE.
2026-03-14T12:08Z - SRE (Samir): Applied connection cap at edge and enabled fallback routing for Acme tenant. Error rate dropped from 8% -> 2% for affected tenant.
2026-03-14T12:32Z - Runtime (Leona): Confirmed runtime emitted repeated prefix eviction traces before OOM; sending heap dumps to infra team.
2026-03-14T13:10Z - Product (Diego): Customer impacted workflows include checkout recommendation and live chat; PR for temporary config change raised (see related_github_prs).
resolution: Mitigation deployed: temporary increase of tenant token bucket and connection cap at edge; fallback to lower-memory model enabled. Root cause under active investigation (runtime eviction strategy + gateway backpressure interaction). Final code fix pending.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigations stabilized customer traffic. Engineering to ship two changes: 1) gateway: support 429 Retry-After advisory header and token-bucket jitter; 2) runtime: adjust KV cache eviction to preferentially trim long-held streaming prefixes during high sync-burst pressure. Target ETA for patch: 2026-03-18. Follow-up postmortem requested and to be linked here when ready.
customer_feedback: Acme support manager called; acknowledged mitigations but requested permanent fix and billing review for retry-inflated usage.
